reasons: Both answers explain the heap vs non-heap gap correctly and recommend MaxRAMPercentage, but B also suggests measuring real memory use (kubectl top, container_memory_working_set_bytes, GC logs), while A only checks the configured MaxHeapSize. A's verification command starts a fresh JVM through kubectl exec, so it would not show the app's actual JAVA_OPTS. Both use some English section headings (Verification/Rollback, Blast Radius), so they are equal on language.

A: The verification command 'kubectl exec <pod> -- java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version' starts a new JVM that does not get the application's JAVA_OPTS, so it does not confirm the app's configured heap.
B: Says kubectl top shows RSS; it actually reports the container working set (minor).
